A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no correlation between FACED and/or BSI scores and systemic inflammation in stable bronchiectosis.
there is a correlation between the FACED and BSA scores and the severity of systemic inflammatory markers such as CRP in patients who have stable bronchiectases.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CRP is a good marker of the severity of inflammation in bronchiectasis and that the BSI score can be used in clinical practice to determine the severity of bronchial inflammation.
FACED and BSA scores can be used as an objective tool to measure the severity and progression of bronchiectatic changes and to monitor the efficacy of the treatment.
CRP levels may be used to assess disease severity in patients with stable chronic bronchiectasis.
